# (PART) Introduction {-}

# Workshop Info

Welcome to the 2026 Large Language Models for Bioinformatics Canadian Bioinformatics Workshop webpage!

**Workshop code:** LLM_Ed-2611 <br>
**Dates:** Saturday–Sunday, November 14–15, 2026 <br>
**Location:** Donadeo Innovation Centre for Engineering (ICE), University of Alberta, Edmonton (in person) <br>
**Workshop listing:** [bioinformatics.ca](https://bioinformatics.ca/workshops-all/2026-large-language-models-for-bioinformatics-edmonton-ab/)

**Travel and venue:** Map, transit, and hotel information is available on the Edmonton logistics page. Weekend building-access details will be emailed closer to the workshop.

## About the Workshop

This two-day workshop focuses on the applications of large language models (LLMs) in bioinformatics. Participants will first be introduced to foundational machine learning (ML) concepts, followed by an in-depth exploration of LLMs and their growing role in bioinformatics. The program includes lectures and hands-on labs covering LLM applications in genomics, proteomics, and natural language processing (NLP). Participants will learn how to use LLMs, and which LLMs to use, for coding in bioinformatics, gene prediction/annotation, protein structure/function analysis, and large-scale literature analysis in their research.

### Course Objectives

After the course, participants should be able to:

- Explain the key concepts of large language models and their applications in bioinformatics, including genomics, proteomics, and general informatics.
- Apply LLMs to perform bioinformatics coding tasks.
- Utilize LLM-based tools for analyzing bioinformatics data in genomics, including gene prediction/annotation, protein structure/function prediction, and large-scale literature analysis.
- Integrate LLMs into bioinformatics workflows for research and analysis.

### Target Audience

Post-doctoral fellows, graduate students, bioinformaticians, computational biologists, and researchers in the life sciences domain, focused on individuals involved in bioinformatics projects with an interest in applying large language models and artificial intelligence to genomics, proteomics, and NLP research.

### Prerequisites

Participants should have a basic understanding of bioinformatics and molecular biology. Familiarity with Python programming and command-line tools is required. Some prior exposure to LLM concepts and tools would be beneficial, though not mandatory.

  .schedule-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; margin: 0 0 2em; }

```{r schedule-data, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(htmltools)
schedule_df <- readr::read_csv(
  "schedule.csv",
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

schedule_table <- function(day_label) {
  day_rows <- schedule_df[schedule_df$day_label == day_label, , drop = FALSE]
  row_tags <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(day_rows))) {
    row_class <- paste0("is-", day_rows$type[[i]])
    row_tags[[i]] <- htmltools::tags$tr(
      class = row_class,
      htmltools::tags$td(day_rows$time_1[[i]], class = "schedule-time"),
      htmltools::tags$td(day_rows$activity[[i]])
    )
  }
  htmltools::tags$div(
    class = "table-responsive",
    htmltools::tags$table(
      class = "schedule-table",
      htmltools::tags$thead(htmltools::tags$tr(
        htmltools::tags$th("Time (MT)", scope = "col"),
        htmltools::tags$th("Activity", scope = "col")
      )),
      do.call(htmltools::tags$tbody, row_tags)
    )
  )
}
```

## Modules

These modules are a tentative grouping of the sessions in the schedule above.

### Module 1: Bioinformatics Data Retrieval

Databases and APIs for DNA, RNA, and protein data, followed by retrieval of
research data from publications. Scheduled on Day 1 at 09:30 and 15:45.

### Module 2: Machine Learning Foundations

Supervised and unsupervised learning, with sequence examples. Scheduled on
Day 1 at 10:45.

### Module 3: Transformers, Embeddings, and Hugging Face

An introduction to transformers and embeddings, followed by a hands-on
Hugging Face session. Scheduled on Day 1 at 13:30 and 14:15.

### Module 4: LLMs for Genomics

An introduction to AlphaGenome. Scheduled on Day 2 at 09:15.

### Module 5: Protein Folding and Interpreting Results

Protein folding with AlphaFold, ColabFold, and ESMFold, followed by guided
interpretation of ColabFold results and discussion. Scheduled on Day 2 from
10:30 to 14:30, with lunch at 12:30.

### Module 6: Capstone and Agentic Coding

Optional supported project work followed by agentic coding. Scheduled on Day 2
at 14:30 and 15:45.
